name: Make
tagline: Visual automation priced by credit, for non-technical teams
description: Visual automation platform that connects thousands of apps in drag-and-drop scenarios, billed by the credit each operation consumes.
priceNote: Pricing as of October 2026; plans change — check the official site.
bestFor: Operations and sales teams that standardize repetitive tasks without a developer
pros: The visual editor is simpler than n8n's and delivers results without writing a single line of code
Credit-based billing makes it explicit what each scenario costs, which helps you defend the investment
Huge app ecosystem with ready-made templates and plenty of learning material circulating in every language
Execution queue with reprocessing, step-by-step history and native tools for handling lists
cons: Every operation on a heavy app burns several credits and consumption grows fast at volume
Heavy processing is a weak point: the tool orchestrates, it does not replace data processing
Scenarios with AI, or apps that call AI in a loop, can burn through the quota in a few days
There is no self-hosted version: the data and the operation live on Make's infrastructure

features.name: Visual scenarios
features.detail: Chained app modules with filters, routers and formulas

features.name: Credit-based plans
features.detail: Each operation deducts credits and the balance is visible in the dashboard

features.name: Thousands of apps
features.detail: Connectors for sales, marketing, databases and WhatsApp

features.name: Loops and aggregators
features.detail: Iterations, tables and native tools for manipulating lists

features.name: Run report
features.detail: Step-by-step history, time spent and reproducible error details

useCases: Register the lead in the CRM and notify the rep in Slack when the website form is submitted
Post ERP invoices taken from the PDFs downloaded to an email folder
Publish the same content to Instagram, LinkedIn and Facebook from an editorial spreadsheet
Cross-check e-commerce orders against the stock sheet and flag mismatches
bestForWho: Small and mid-sized companies with repetitive, standardizable processes and no developer on the team.
verdict: Make is the easiest option to put into production when nobody in the company can code, and the scenario canvas is more intuitive than n8n's. The trade-off is the credit model, which cuts both ways: a scenario that syncs the CRM with a spreadsheet can burn half the quota in a week without anyone noticing. The biggest risk is not the plan price, it is the flow design, because a badly built step multiplies operations and turns into a high bill with no warning. For a small company, the Core plan with 10,000 credits covers the essentials and lets you monitor consumption scenario by scenario. For a larger company, weigh the Teams plan for its role-based access controls, but do the credit math before you migrate any critical process.
